Present:
 Mr. D.N. Sharma, Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. Pankaj Joshi, A.G.A. for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.(Oral)

Instant appeal is preferred against the judgment and order dated 07.10.2025, passed in Special Sessions Trial No. 264 of 2021, State of Uttarakhand Vs. Mukesh, by the court of Additional Sessions Judge/FTSC, Rudrapur, District Udham Singh Nagar.

By it, the appellant has been acquitted of the charge under Section 366, 376 (2- n) IPC and Section 5/6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and convicted and sentenced under Section 363 IPC.

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
Admit.

4. Call for the LCR.
5.
After receipt of the LCR.
Let paper book be prepared and provided to learned counsel for the parties, as per Rules.
6. List in due course.

Heard on Bail Application No. 1 of 2025 Mukesh vs State Of Uttarakhand on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8243844/
1
7. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has been convicted for three years imprisonment.
He was in custody during trial for more than 18 months.
Thereafter, he was on bail during trial.
He is still on interim bail.
He has never misused the bail.
8. Learned State counsel admits these facts.
9. Having considered, without adverting much on merits, this Court is of the view it is a case in which the execution of sentence should be suspended and the appellant be enlarged on bail.

10. The bail application is allowed.
11.
The sentence appealed against is suspended during the pendency of the appeal.

12. The appellant be released on bail, during the pendency of the appeal, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned.

(Ravindra Maithani, J.) 06.11.2025 Jitendra Mukesh vs State Of Uttarakhand on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8243844/
